Laguna Hedionda is part of a route through Bolivia's high-altitude lakes and lagoons. The itinerary combines a visit here with stops at the Cañapa and Honda lagoons.

Along the way, volcanic landscapes unfold across the Lípez region. At the lagoons, travelers can observe Andean flamingos before continuing toward the Siloli Desert.

Laguna Honda is included in the journey through Bolivia's highlands. Travelers visit it while crossing the Lípez region on the way to the Siloli Desert.

This stop is paired with the Cañapa and Hedionda lagoons. The route takes visitors past open bodies of water, volcanic landscapes and places where Andean flamingos can be observed.

At Laguna Miñiques, the water is surrounded by a dry high-altitude landscape. Pale shores and volcanic slopes make it stand out amid the desert scenery of the Atacama.

Miñiques and Miscanti are part of Los Flamencos National Reserve. A visit to the lagoons can be combined with Socaire before continuing to the salt flat and Laguna Chaxa.

At Miscanti, dark water contrasts with the dry slopes of the Andes. The lagoon is visited together with neighboring Miñiques on trips from San Pedro de Atacama.

Both lagoons are part of Los Flamencos National Reserve. Their high-altitude landscapes can be combined with a stop in Socaire and a visit to the Atacama Salt Flat.
